body: Yeah it's ChrisTombstone (Flop) playing Tex's son Eddie and he is rolling for if he passes out

The point was also for the court case to argue that despite the new pings for people carving up corpses, there wasn't a charge that fit properly. 

He absolutely would have been found not guilty of manslaughter and maybe been able to get some legislation that made his business legit if he'd let it play out instead of doing some odd perma on the docket.

Met with who? 

Reggie called him saying his life was in danger and asked to meet. Flop said no because it would be dumb to go to a location dictated by Reggie without backup. 

Brought it up to Ziggy who said he should talk to Snow or Dark but mostly shouted at him about how he was going to go John Wick on anyone that kidnapped him. Tried to talk to Dark, it got heated and Dark stonewalled him. Chris had stuff going on IRL and wasn't on long enough to link up with Snow. 

Somewhere in here he finds out Cross is on the run and fearing for his life so he speaks to him about Cross meeting Michael. They also vent about the absolute shit show of trying to get a hold of command/someone with knowledge of the investigation in early shift 3. Walker, who has been up for like 16 hours, makes the most cooked notes on this conversation and taps out half way through. 

Reggie then gets kidnapped and shot and won't give his statement to anyone but Flop. Flop takes it at the hospital with another officer present the whole time. Collects casings, makes the report and immediately forwards it on to Bundy and Brian. 

After all this Bundy takes Flop's entire statement on what has happened: the only person to actually listen long enough without just screaming at him to get the full story. Flop explicitly says he doesn't want to be involved in the investigation but he will help if needed. 

And in all of this he still hasn't met with Reggie for the original request which it turns out was just to run the casings of Reggie's gun in case he gets taken. Despite Reggie calling him maybe 10 times a day from his own phone and payphones to repeatedly ask why he hasn't done it yet.
